thread:
oncall-bot: High-severity alert: multiple GPU OOMs + CrashLoopBackOffs detected in eu-west inference pool during autoscale event. Paging @oncall. (alert_id: INCD-2249-euw)
Alex Chen: saw it, I'm on it. Starting triage. Can someone post tail of kube events and the autoscaler logs? :mag:
Jess Rivera: quick context — we had a traffic spike at 14:18 UTC, autoscaler did a rapid scale-up, then nodes started OOMing during model init. Some pods restarted repeatedly. I think it's a capacity thrash + memory spike in the runtime.
Maria Gomez: logs: kubelet shows OOMKilled and container runtime restart loop. snippet:
```
14:20:11 kubelet: Pod model-serve-5f6d OOMKilled (oom_score_adj=0)
14:20:12 containerd: restarting container model-serve-5f6d (CrashLoopBackOff)
14:20:34 autoscaler: scaleUp: +10 nodes requested, provisioned 8, 2 timed out
```
Jess Rivera: here's `kubectl get pods` output for the failing subset:
```
NAME                       READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
model-serve-5f6d            0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6          12m
model-serve-7c9a            0/1     OOMKilled          3          11m
model-serve-9b2f            1/1     Running            0          9m
```
Sanjay Patel: hypothesis: autoscaler brought nodes up too quickly, scheduler batched a lot of cold KV cache warmups onto the new GPUs which caused memory pressure. Also saw CUDA driver warnings in nodes that were reused from previous workloads.
Alex Chen: agree. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) damp autoscaler (increase stabilization window), 2) patch model deployment to limit init parallelism and add startup probe delays, 3) roll traffic to smaller quantized variant, 4) cordon + drain repeatedly-failing nodes.
Linda Park: customer impact check: our SLOs show a regional spike in 5xxs between 14:20-14:34 UTC. Approx 8% of requests retried/errored. Affected routes: /v1/generate (models: rwd-large-v2 default). Top impacted tenants: "search-ops", "chatlytics" (both on Dedicated eu-west pools). We're classifying as partial degradation. Customer success already notified for the high-traffic tenants.
Maria Gomez: starting graceful traffic shift. Taking model rwd-large-v2 -> rwd-large-v2-quantized-fallback on eu-west nodes. Triggering canary with 10% traffic.
deploy-bot: rolling update started: route split applied -> rwd-large-v2-quantized-fallback (10%) | rwd-large-v2 (90%). Job: route-split/224902
Jess Rivera: while canary runs, I'm applying a temporary patch to the cluster-autoscaler config to increase "scaleDownUnneededTime" and add a 60s delay to scale-up aggressiveness. Patch:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: Config
spec:
  scaleUp:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
  scaleDown:
    unneededTime: 300
```
Sanjay Patel: also patching deployment env to limit parallel init threads: `MODEL_INIT_PARALLEL=2` and setting startupProbe to 60s so nodes don't overload on bootstrap.
Alex Chen: cordon plan: identify nodes with repeated OOMs and cordon+drain with `--delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets`. Maria, can you list the node IDs you want drained?
Maria Gomez: draining nodes: euw-node-gpu-17, euw-node-gpu-21 (both show repeated cuda errors). Running:
```
kubectl cordon euw-node-gpu-17 && kubectl drain euw-node-gpu-17 --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets
```
Ops note: observed CUDA errors before crash: `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` and `cuda out of memory` in dmesg.
Linda Park: notifications: CS notified for premium tenants at 14:30 UTC, status page updated to "degraded" for eu-west inference. ETA to recovery estimated 30-45m depending on rollouts.
Alex Chen: current status: canary traffic to quantized fallback showing 0 OOMs in canary pods so far (3m). Overall 5xx rate trending down from 8% -> 2.5%.
Sanjay Patel: we should also pin future autoscaler rollups to smaller batch sizes; adding a cluster-level admission webhook to limit new pod parallelism for model inits is a medium-term follow-up.
deploy-bot: rollback option ready: can revert route split if canary has any failures. Command: `rwdctl routes revert route-split/224902`
Jess Rivera: creating incident runbook entry and recording the commands we ran. Short-term action items gonna be in the incident doc.
Alex Chen: handing off to next oncall in 25m. Next-oncall: Jess Rivera. Current actions for handoff: continue traffic canary -> 50% over next 10m, monitor OOMs, complete node drains, keep autoscaler damped.
Jess Rivera: ack, taking over. Will also follow up with infra team to validate CUDA driver versions on node pool (possible mismatch). Will open a ticket with cluster infra for node image rebuild if needed.
Linda Park: summary for postmortem: root cause likely autoscale-induced parallel cold KV/cache warmups + hot model init patterns on new nodes -> memory pressure and CUDA driver instability; contributing factors: aggressive scale-up policy + no init parallelism controls. Impact: regional partial degradation, ~8% request errors at peak, high-traffic tenants affected. Action items: autoscaler tuning, init parallelism control, fallback model routing defaults, node image validation.
Alex Chen: closing note: we've stabilized the region, ongoing monitoring for 1h. If anything regresses, escalate immediately. :thumbsup:
